features.headline: Premier League VAR review: Should Man United's equalizing goal have been allowed?
features.desc: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
body: The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.
Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship.

With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday.
Referee: Chris Kavanagh VAR: Craig Pawson Time: 96 minutes Incident: Possible foul in Manchester United's equalizing goal.
What happened: Bruno Fernandes swung in a last-chance corner kick as Man United threw every player they had on the pitch, including keeper Senne Lammens, into the penalty area.
Patrick Dorgu outjumped the Aston Villa defenders and, with keeper Zion Suzuki flapping at the ball, nodded home what seemed like a straightforward header into the net.

However, Suzuki believed he was fouled by opposite number Lammens as the United No. 1 attempted to block the Villa keeper — Lammens made contact with Suzuki while neither looking at the ball nor making any attempt to play it.
Referee Kavanagh was unmoved by the appeals, yellow-carding Suzuki for his protests and awarding the goal.

features.headline: Which player has the most career points in NHL history?
features.desc: Wayne Gretzky leads the list of NHL players with the most career points. Check out other top performers now.
body: Wayne Gretzky owns a laundry list of NHL records, including the mark for the most career points.
A player earns a point by either scoring a goal or getting an assist, which is credited to up to two players who pass the puck toward a teammate who scores.
Gretzky's 894 career goals plus his 1,963 career assists give him a grand total of 2,857 points over his illustrious 20-year career. That's nearly 1,000 more than any other player.

features.headline: Week 9 winners and losers: Lamb, Walker come up big, Gibbs, Taylor disappoint
features.desc: CeeDee Lamb and Kenneth Walker III came up big in Week 9, while Jahmyr Gibbs and Jonathan Taylor were quieter than usual.
features.by: Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft
body: Week 9 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured another big performance from the Cincinnati Bengals' trio of Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, as well as massive days by Kenneth Walker III, CeeDee Lamb and Puka Nacua.
Things didn't go quite as well for Jahmyr Gibbs, Jonathan Taylor and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who fell short of their normal standard Sunday.
So, who were the big winners and losers around the league? Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.
Jump to a topic: Ranking winners | Ranking losers Biggest injuries and what's next
Walker scored a season-high 36.3 points in Sunday's win over the Jets, his third game of 30 or more points this season. Walker had 143 total yards and three touchdowns on 24 touches.
While Walker had two subpar games this season (SEA, DEN), he remains the most consistent fantasy scorer in the Chiefs' offense. — Bowen
CB Christian Gonzalez and the Patriots' defense couldn't contain Green Bay, as QB Jordan Love and WRs Matthew Golden and Christian Watson all exceeded 30 fantasy points in the Packers' 45-27 victory.
Golden and Watson each had at least 160 yards and a touchdown receiving, becoming the first wide receiver teammates since Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle in Week 2 of 2022 to do that in the same game.
The two wideouts totaled 10 catches for 187 yards and two scores with Gonzalez as the nearest defender, per Next Gen Stats.
Love, meanwhile, scored a career-high 36.18 fantasy points, throwing for 235 yards and a score on deep throws (at least 20 yards downfield).

features.headline: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
features.desc: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
body: In his first game since Week 1, Garrett made his presence felt. He had three sacks to move ahead of Dwight Freeney, Derrick Thomas and Rickey Jackson for 18th on the list. He was the only one of the active leaders to record a sack this week.
With two players on bye and Garrett out, only two of the five active players that played this week recorded sacks, but they were impactful.
Miller recorded his first sack as a Cowboy Sunday, moving him ahead of Terrell Suggs and into a tie with Jason Taylor for seventh.
Watt added two sacks of his own, moving him ahead of Simeon Rice and Clyde Simmons for 23rd. He now has 7.5 sacks on the season.
Hunter and Watt were the only ones to record sacks this week, with Hunter jumping back over Campbell in the rankings.
With Garrett still out, it was another quiet week on the sack front. Of the active leaders, it was the oldest that recorded the lone sack of the week in Campbell. He moved back in front of Hunter.
Hunter was the only player among the active leaders to record a sack this week, moving him ahead of Campbell to No. 26 all-time. Hunter now has three sacks through five games.

Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR.
There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list.

features.headline: Jets begin to unravel on and off field as losing streak hits 4 games
features.desc: New York players were seen slamming helmets during their 35-12 loss in Kansas City, where they failed to score a TD.
body: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — Every losing season has different stages. At first, there's defiance, which turns to frustration, which often becomes resignation. It's not pretty to watch.
The New York Jets hit Stage 2 on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium, where their most memorable throws of the day involved helmets, not footballs.
An enraged Geno Smith threw his helmet at the bench after a fourth-down sack in the fourth quarter of the Jets' 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
A short time later, right tackle Armand Membou lost his cool and spiked his helmet on the field after allowing a sack to Chris Jones — an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.
This is what the Jets have become: a 2-7 team, losers of four straight, seemingly out of answers — and coming unglued before our eyes.
The root of the frustration: They failed to score a touchdown Sunday despite 32 offensive plays in Chiefs' territory — their most in plus territory without a TD since Week 3 in the 2022 season.
Asked why they're struggling to reach the end zone, running back Breece Hall deadpanned, "I mean, that's been [the case for] the last however many years we've been here."

If coach Aaron Glenn has any chance of saving his job — with a 5-21 record, it looks bleak — he needs to stave off the resignation stage. That's when it gets really ugly, when the energy is drained out of the locker room, when fissures form among players. It's when hope is gone.

Presumably, Glenn will have the final eight games to convince owner Woody Johnson that the organization is heading in the right direction under his leadership. It could be an insurmountable challenge.

features.headline: What Yankees, Mets can do this winter to meet their 2027 goals
features.desc: The 2026 MLB season didn't go as either New York team planned. Here's how they can flip the script next year.
body: With a lockout looming on Dec. 1, the consensus across Major League Baseball is that November will be a frenetic month, similar to the lead-up to the 2021 lockout. Free agents will come off the board. Trades will be made. There will be a flurry of player movement before the league shuts down.

The action, according to sources, is expected to start as soon as next week, when the industry convenes at the general managers meetings in Las Vegas. And you can expect the two New York clubs will be involved.

The Yankees and Mets experienced very different versions of disappointment in 2026. The Yankees reached the postseason for the eighth time in nine years under manager Aaron Boone, only to get bounced by an American League East rival in the division series for the second straight year.
The Mets, meanwhile, did not make the playoffs for the second consecutive season, finishing last in the National League East despite having one of baseball's two most expensive payrolls.

Both teams will dabble in the free agent and trade markets to bolster their rosters this offseason. Here are three needs we believe each team will address to get over the hump by the time Opening Day comes around — whenever that is.
1. Rebuild the bullpen (starting with closer David Bednar?)

Pitching was not the problem for the Yankees in 2026. They led the majors in staff ERA by a good margin. But while they have a surplus of starters, they'll need to fill out their bullpen again this offseason.
As it stands, left-hander Brent Headrick is the only reliever under team control for next season who had at least 17 appearances in 2026.
